simulation.offset.invalid: Time must be a whole number of milliseconds.
simulation.mech.9.body: Rules are kept in the project file, never in the OSB; exported storyboards and videos are not affected.
simulation.mech.8.body: In play an event happens on the frame the player actually hits, with their timing error; missed objects raise nothing; pass/fail depends on health. This simulation uses the exact moments the rules give and does not compute health. Beatmap events are approximate for taiko, catch and mania, and spinner bonuses are not raised.
simulation.mech.7.body: Each rule sets one of lazer's values at a moment: a HitSound rule the set of samples just played, a HitObjectHit rule the latest judgement, a Pass/Fail rule whether the player is passing. A beatmap-events rule raises HitSound and HitObjectHit for the shown difficulty as if every object were hit perfectly. Only ticked rules take effect after Confirm; ticking none turns triggers off.
simulation.mech.7: How rules stand for the game
simulation.mech.6.body: They coexist; neither excludes the other. Pass/fail is one global state that starts Passing (taiko starts Failing and turns Passing once health passes half). It decides whether the Pass or the Fail layer is shown, and fires Passing or Failing triggers the moment it changes. HitSound and HitObjectHit triggers fire whatever the state, on sprites of a hidden layer too; when the layer shows again, its sprites look as they should at that moment. Storyboard sounds of a hidden layer do not play.
simulation.mech.5.body: A sprite exists only while its own commands and loops say so: what a trigger does outside that time is not seen, and a sprite with nothing but triggers is never shown. Give it an ordinary command (such as an F at opacity 0) to set when it exists.
simulation.mech.4.body: Each firing schedules the commands again. A newly scheduled command removes every later command of the same property, the sprite's own commands included, and cuts off one of that property still running when it starts. Firing again therefore restarts rather than adds up, and an F in a trigger cancels the sprite's later F commands, such as a fade-out at its end. Triggers do not exclude each other, and the group number is not used.
simulation.mech.3.body: HitSound[normal bank][addition bank][addition][index]. A bank is All, Normal, Soft or Drum; All or nothing means any. With a single bank followed by an addition (HitSoundSoftClap) the bank is the addition's. The number at the end is the custom sample index (the 2 of soft-hitclap2.wav); indexes 0 and 1 have no suffix, so HitSound1 never fires. A slider tick is a HitSound too, and the normal bank does not restrict it.
simulation.mech.2.body:
- HitSound: a hit object is hit and its sound plays, with the whole set of samples played (normal sound, additions, their banks and index).
- HitObjectHit: a successful, scored judgement (not a miss). A slider's head, ticks, repeats and tail count once each.
- Passing / Failing: the moment the pass/fail state changes. Setting the state it already has fires nothing.
The osu! slider tail judgement can occur 36 ms early, after previous nested judgements; its sound stays at the end. Slider ticks and catch droplets take their bank and index from the green line at the slider's start. Catch bananas also raise HitSound, carrying the spinner's normal sample (hitnormal with its bank and index).
simulation.mech.1.body: Commands under T,condition,start,end[,group] do not run on their own. When the game raises an event that meets the condition at a moment inside the [start, end] window (both ends included; left out means no limit), they run once, counting their times from that moment. This simulation follows osu!lazer exactly.

Software encoding on the CPU works on any machine and gives the best picture for a bit rate, but is the slowest.
Hardware encoding on a graphics card, dedicated or integrated, is much faster, with a slightly lesser picture for the same bit rate.
videoexport.bitrate.name: Video bit rate
videoexport.bitrate.tip:
When off, the bit rate recommended for the resolution, frame rate and codec is used.
A higher bit rate gives a better picture and a larger file. It is an average: busy stretches get more of it.
videoexport.audioBitrate.tip:
The bit rate of the sound in the video: AAC in MP4, MKV and FLV, MP3 in AVI. Type it, or pick it from the list at the right.
The most AAC can have depends on the sample rate (529 kbps at 44.1 kHz); MP3 only has a fixed set of bit rates.
videoexport.sampleRate.tip:
The sample rate of the sound in the video, which is stereo. Type it, or pick it from the list at the right.
The main audio, the replacement audio and the storyboard samples are each brought to this rate
straight from the rate of their own file, once; what has this rate already is not converted at all.
AAC takes the standard rates from 7350 to 96000 Hz, the MP3 of an AVI only those from 8000 to 48000 Hz.
videoexport.music.replace.tip:
Puts another audio file into the video in place of the project's main audio, such as the lossless version of the song (FLAC, WAV, APE, ALAC…): the sound of the video is then encoded straight from the lossless source rather than from the beatmap's MP3 a second time.
This only affects the exported video; the project, the preview and the exported .osb stay as they are. Storyboard samples are mixed in as ever.
Once a file is chosen it is lined up with the main audio by itself.

videoexport.music.delay.tip:
How many milliseconds later than the timeline the replacement audio begins; negative for earlier.
The value found automatically puts it exactly where the main audio is in the preview. A decoded MP3 is usually some tens of milliseconds behind its lossless source, so this is mostly a small positive number; if the beatmap's audio had its beginning cut off, it is a negative one.
Type a value to set it by hand.

dialog.clash.title: Check before saving
clash.title: Cannot be added here
clash.add:
"{0}" and "{1}" cannot be in effect at the same time: they are about the same thing, and osu! lets only one of them have its way at any moment.

At {2} the two would overlap, so nothing was added.

Keep their times apart: add it after the other one has ended (or before it begins), or delete the stretch that overlaps first.
track.blocked:
"{0}" has another command of its kind running at {1}, unseen under the one that began first.
Setting a value at this moment would mean cutting the command that has its way in two here, and the second half would then be hidden by that other command, which changes the picture from here on. So nothing was changed.

Move the playhead to where one of the commands begins or ends and adjust there, or take the overlap away first: drag the commands apart in the timeline, or change their times in the Properties panel.
loop.outside:
The playhead is not within this loop ({0} – {1}).
The commands of a loop repeat in every pass: what the preview adjusts is the moment of the pass the playhead is in, and every pass changes with it.
Move the playhead into the loop and adjust there.
clash.pair.scale: S scale and V vector scale
clash.save.count: Commands overlap in time in {0} place(s).
clash.save.text: The position M cannot be in effect together with MX / MY, nor the scale S together with the vector scale V: osu! lets only one of them have its way at any moment, and the picture in the game will differ from this preview.
clash.save.hint: Click a line (or "Go to the first") to select that object and move the playhead to where the overlap begins; nothing is saved or exported this time. The timeline marks the stretch in red under the property rows.
problems.errors.tip:
Includes commands that could not be parsed and were skipped, and M versus MX / MY or S versus V conflicts.
Source records retain errors from reading; current command conflicts are checked again as you edit.
problems.warnings.tip:
What is probably not meant, though the game and the preview agree about it:
commands of one kind that overlap in time, commands that end before they start,
files that are not in the assets folder.
problems.noneListed: No problems to list with the filter as it is.
problems.clash.tip:
These two kinds of command are in effect at the same time over this stretch, and they are about the same thing:
osu! lets only one of them have its way at any moment, so the picture in the game differs from this preview.
Keep their times apart, or delete the stretch that overlaps.
problems.overlap.tip:
Commands of one kind are in effect at the same time over this stretch.
osu! lets the one that began first have its way until it ends; the later one does nothing before that.
The preview shows it the same way, but it is seldom what was meant.
Such a property cannot be shown as keyframes in the timeline; its commands are edited as they are written.
problems.reversed.tip:
This command ends before it starts.
osu! and the preview both take it to happen all at once at its start time.
problems.locate.tip: Click to select the object and go to the property and the commands the problem is about.

props.groupButton.tip: Puts the selected sprites, animations and groups into a new group. It is one row in the timeline, to be moved, scaled, rotated, shifted in time and trimmed as a whole; double-click it to go in and edit what is in it
props.name: Name
props.name.tip: Used only in the editor; it is not written to the exported .osb
props.groupPosition.tip:
Where the pivot appears in the picture. Changing it moves the whole group, including its existing move commands.
The group's members can also be dragged in the preview.
props.pivot.tip: Members rotate and scale around this point. Changing only the pivot does not move the members (at times when the group is neither rotated nor scaled).
props.member.tip: Click to go into the group and select this member
props.addMemberNote: To add a member: go into the group and add or paste it there, or select a sprite and choose the group in its properties.
props.bake.nested: Nested precision: {0} ms, {1} px · the stricter group settings apply
props.bake.step.tip:
osu! has no groups: on export the motion of a group is written as commands of each member, arcs and curves cut into straight pieces.
No piece is cut shorter than this many milliseconds. A larger number means fewer commands; very fast motion then shows its corners.
The preview shows what comes out at this precision, as the game plays it.
props.bake.tolerance.tip:
How many pixels a position may be off the motion it follows; scale and rotation by as much as comes to the same (0.5 pixels: 0.3% of scale, 0.17° of rotation).
A larger number means fewer commands and a less rounded motion.
Where motion is so fast that it is off by more within the shortest step, the shortest step decides.
props.bake.count: The {0} members of this group are exported as {1} commands at this precision.
props.bake.reset: Back to the default ({0} ms, {1} px)
props.relativeToBlock: (times are relative to the start of the block)
props.degrees.tip: Rotation is shown and typed in degrees; the file always stores radians
props.groupEmpty:
No keyframes yet: the members are shown by their own keyframes.
A group only has position (M/MX/MY), scale (S) and rotation (R). On export they are expanded into each member's own commands.
props.firstFrameMissing: The first frame {0} was not found
props.fileMissing: This file is not in the assets folder
props.owner.tip: The file this object's script is written to. The shared storyboard shows in every difficulty; an object of one difficulty shows in that difficulty only, and is drawn behind the shared ones.
props.joinGroup.tip: A member of a group follows the group's movement, scale and rotation; its own commands still apply.
props.initialPosition.tip: The x,y of the declaration. Where the position (M/MX/MY) has keyframes, those count.
props.beatmapBg.description: Hides the default in-game background to reduce redundant drawing and SB Load. The path must match this difficulty's background image.
props.beatmapBg.pathOnly: Beatmap BG only supports changing the image path. Keep the Sprite,Background,TopLeft,"image path",0,0 format.
props.addKey.tip:
Adds or selects this command type at the playhead using the object's current value.
Then adjust its time, easing and values.
props.filter.tip:
When on, the panel shows only the part that is picked in the timeline:
a property row (F opacity, say): its keyframes alone
a loop or trigger: all that is in it
a property row of a loop: the keyframes of that property in that loop
the object itself: everything
When off, the whole object is shown at all times.
props.filter.all.tip: Lets go of the property or loop that is picked and goes back to the whole object.
props.addKey.blockTip:
Adds or selects this command type at the playhead using the object's current value.
Times count from the start of the loop or trigger; with the playhead ahead of it, the command is added at its start.
props.key.tip:
Click to select this keyframe; it is highlighted in the timeline, and its property becomes the one that dragging the object in the preview adjusts.
Double-click: move the playhead here
props.key.time: Time of the keyframe (between the one before it and the one after it)
props.key.easing: How the value gets from this keyframe to the next one: {0}
props.key.last.tip:
No keyframe comes after this one, so there is no transition to choose.
Add another keyframe at a later time and this can be chosen.
props.track.clash.tip:
These two kinds of command are in effect at the same time, and osu! lets only one of them have its way.
The timeline marks the stretch in red under this row; keep their times apart, or delete one of the two.
props.track.raw.tip:
Several commands of this property run at the same time, so it has no single value at a moment and cannot be shown as keyframes.
The commands can be changed here or in the Script panel.
Where they lie over one another in the timeline, a click selects the shortest, and another click at the same spot the next one.
The property can still be picked and adjusted by dragging in the preview: that changes the command that has its way at the playhead.
props.noCommands: No keyframes yet. An object is only shown between its first and its last keyframe.
props.onlyTriggers: Only trigger commands: add ordinary commands to define the sprite's lifetime.
props.neverShown: No commands: the object is never shown
props.command.tip: Click to select; the command is highlighted in the timeline
easing.hold: No transition: the value stays as it is and becomes the next one all at once.
easing.in: Slow at first, then faster and faster.
easing.out: Fast at first, then slower and slower.
easing.inOut: Slow at both ends, fast in between.
easing.strength: From the gentlest to the sharpest: {0}
easing.back.in: Draws back a little first, then goes.
easing.back.out: Goes a little too far, then comes back.
easing.back.inOut: Draws back first, goes too far and comes back.
easing.elastic.in: Swings to and fro like a spring first, then goes.
easing.elastic.out: Goes, then swings to and fro like a spring until it settles.
easing.elastic.inOut: Swings like a spring at both ends.
easing.bounce.in: Bounces higher and higher like a ball, and lands on the end value.
easing.bounce.out: Lands and bounces a few times like a ball before it rests.
easing.bounce.inOut: Bounces like a ball at both ends.
curve.about: A curve of your own, which goes through each of its points.
curve.about.groups: Only the commands of a group can have one; exported as plain osb commands.
curve.hint: Ctrl+click adds a point · drag moves it · right-click removes it
curve.hint.more:
The curve goes through every point; its two ends stay where they are.
Near the lines of the start and the end value a point lands on them, unless Alt is held.
Beyond the two lines the value goes past where it starts or ends, and comes back.
props.startTime: Start time (cannot be after the end time)
props.endTime: End time (cannot be before the start time)
props.paramWhole: Same start and end: applies for as long as the object is shown
props.copyValue: Make the end value the same as the start value
props.loopNote: {0} ms per pass; the times of keyframes count from 0 at the start of each pass
props.triggerIndexNoSuffix: In lazer indexes 0 and 1 have no suffix, so this condition would never fire.
props.triggerIndexLeadingZero: lazer compares suffixes as text: {0} is not {1}.
props.triggerIndexDigits: The index must be a whole number of up to 9 digits.
props.triggerOneAddition: A lazer condition can name only one addition.
props.triggerZeroWindow: Window is 0,0: lazer accepts events only at 0 ms. Tick "No limit" to accept them all the time.
props.triggerOnlySprite: The sprite has nothing but triggers: lazer never shows it. Give it an ordinary command (such as an F at opacity 0).
props.triggerNoRules: No rule in use fires it.
props.triggerNotSimulated: Not simulated: no rule is ticked. Command times count from the window start.
props.triggerRelative: Command times count from the firing (this one at {0})
props.triggerRelativeNone: Command times count from the firing (not simulated; from the window start {0})
props.triggerAdjustRefused: Make this trigger fire in the trigger simulation before adjusting it in the preview.
props.triggerCondition.tip: Choose HitSound, HitObjectHit, Passing or Failing, or one of the common conditions. The HitSound fields match the simulation's HitSound rule.
props.triggerStartTime: Trigger start time (cannot be after the end time)
props.triggerEndTime: Trigger end time (cannot be before the start time)
props.sampleLayer.tip: A sample on the Pass or Fail layer only plays in that state
props.videoTime.tip: The moment the video starts playing; may be negative (the second field of the Video line in the script)
props.videoNote: A video takes no commands: it plays under every layer and over the background, centred and filling the picture, fading in over its first second and out over its last (as in osu!).
time.offGrid: Not on a snap tick (a typed value)
time.tip: Click: type any time in ms   Drag: move by ticks   Right-click: more
viewer.fit.tip: Fits the picture to the window (the wheel zooms, a middle-button or Alt+left drag pans)
viewer.state.tip: Whether the preview shows the Pass layer or the Fail layer
viewer.dim.tip: Works like background dim in osu!: the beatmap background and every storyboard layer are darkened together (the osu! editor always uses 30%). Preview only, never exported
viewer.outside.tip: Shows what lies outside the picture faintly, which helps while building. When off, only the finished picture is shown: nothing outside it is drawn or can be picked
viewer.hitObjects.tip:
Shows the selected difficulty's circles, sliders and spinners between the Foreground and Overlay layers.
All objects are hit on time and use the skin selected in the toolbar. Background dim leaves them unchanged; screenshots and exported videos use the selected skin too.
hitobjects.noDifficulties: The referenced beatmap directory has no available .osu files; only the shared storyboard is shown. Link a beatmap directory in project settings.
hitobjects.noneSelected: The shared storyboard is shown now. Choose a difficulty at the top right of the preview.
hitobjects.otherMode: This difficulty uses an unsupported game mode.
viewer.videoProblem.tip: Select the video in the Video section of the timeline to change its file; the View menu turns the video off if it is not needed.
video.missing: The video file {0} is not among the assets. It shows once it has been added (drop it on the window).
video.noDecoder: the video decoding libraries (FFmpeg) that come with the program are missing from its folder or cannot be loaded
video.noPicture: the file has no video that can be decoded
video.stuck: the video decoder does not respond
viewer.emptyHint: Drag an image here from the Assets panel, or write commands in the Script panel
viewer.difficulty.tip:
Difficulty shown: {0}
The storyboard of this .osu is drawn together with the shared one (.osb). osu! loads the .osu before the .osb, so the .osu's objects are drawn behind. Background, widescreen and BPM follow this difficulty too.
viewer.sharedOnly.tip: Shows only the storyboard all difficulties share (.osb). Pick a difficulty (.osu) here to see its own storyboard along with it.
viewer.screenshot.tip: Screenshot: save the picture of this moment as an image
viewer.screenshot.title: Screenshot size
viewer.screenshot.note: Only the storyboard picture is saved, without guides and selection frames.
viewer.currentTime.tip: The current time in ms. Click to type any time; drag to move by snap ticks.
viewer.rate.tip: Type any speed from {0} to {1}×, or pick a usual one from the list.
viewer.rate.invalid: The playback speed must be from {0} to {1}.
viewer.rate.precision: The playback speed can have at most 3 decimals.
timeline.snap.tip:
Beat snap divisor. With snapping on, dragging, seeking and creating on the timeline all align to these ticks;
with snapping off, or by typing a time, a time can be off them.
timeline.snapOn.tip:
On: the playhead, bars and keyframes that are dragged, and whatever is created, align to the snap ticks.
Off (free mode): any millisecond will do. Some imported storyboards have their commands at times that are not on a tick; with snapping off those can be dragged a little, and the playhead can stand between two ticks.
The arrow keys go on moving the playhead from tick to tick; to stand exactly on a keyframe, use the previous / next keyframe buttons of the player.
viewer.previousKey.tip:
Go to the previous keyframe (Ctrl+←)
With a property picked, from keyframe to keyframe of that property; otherwise of everything the selected objects or groups have.
The playhead lands exactly on the keyframe, on a tick or not.
viewer.nextKey.tip:
Go to the next keyframe (Ctrl+→)
With a property picked, from keyframe to keyframe of that property; otherwise of everything the selected objects or groups have.
The playhead lands exactly on the keyframe, on a tick or not.
status.keyJumpNothing: Select an object, a group or a property first to go from keyframe to keyframe of it
status.keyJumpNone: What is selected has no keyframes
status.keyJumpEnd: There are no more keyframes that way
shortcut.keyJump: Go to the previous / next keyframe (of the picked property, or all keyframes of what is selected)
timeline.noBpm.tip: Without a BPM there are no snap ticks and times cannot be aligned. Enter the BPM and the offset in File > Project settings.
timeline.zoomIn.tip:
Zoom in a small step, keeping the current time in place.
Alt+wheel (or Ctrl+wheel) over the tracks also zooms the timeline.
timeline.zoomOut.tip: Zoom out a small step, keeping the current time in place.
timeline.snapThinned: At this zoom only some of the ticks are drawn; zoom in to see every one.
timeline.ownOnly.tip:
Lists only the objects that belong to the shown difficulty alone (.osu), to make them easy to edit.
The preview stays as it is: the shared storyboard's objects are still drawn.
timeline.showingOnly.tip:
Lists only the objects that are being rendered at this moment: sprites and animations whose commands span the current time (also when transparent or off the screen just now), and videos that are playing.
The list follows playback and seeking; the preview stays as it is. Selected objects are always listed. Of Pass and Fail only the layer of the state the preview shows counts; sounds are not listed.
timeline.key.add: Add a keyframe at the playhead
timeline.value.edit: Double-click to edit this keyframe value. Enter confirms; Escape cancels. Separate multiple values with commas.
timeline.value.colour.edit: Double-click to open the colour picker for this keyframe. Adjust the colour or enter RGB, HSV or Hex. Confirm keeps changes; Cancel, Escape or clicking outside restores the original colour.
timeline.value.colour.format: Enter a colour as #RRGGBB or #RGB, or R, G, B (0–255).
timeline.track.tip:
Click to pick this property, click again to let go of it.
While it is picked, dragging anywhere in the preview adjusts the selected object at the playhead; hitting its pixels is not required, and a keyframe is added if there is none.
Opacity: drag up and down
Position: drag anywhere (MX only sideways, MY only up and down)
Scale: drag up and down
Vector scale: sideways for the width, up and down for the height
Rotation: up turns clockwise, down anticlockwise
With no property picked, dragging an object moves it as a whole.
timeline.track.loopTip: This is a property of a loop: it can be adjusted with the playhead in any pass, which changes that moment of the loop in every pass. The playhead has to be within the loop.
timeline.track.pickTip:
Click to pick this property; click again to let go of it.
Picked, it is what the Properties panel shows alone (while "Show only what is picked" is on).
It cannot be adjusted by dragging in the preview: flipping and additive blending are on or off, and a trigger runs when the game says so, which the preview does not play.
timeline.block.tip: Click to select the whole loop (or trigger). Delete then removes it rather than the sprite; it can be dragged in the tracks.
timeline.key.remove: Delete this keyframe at the playhead
timeline.lock.tip: A locked object cannot be selected or dragged in the preview
timeline.leaveGroup.tip: Leave this group, one step out (Esc does the same while nothing is selected)
timeline.group.tip:
A group: what is in it, as one thing. Its members stay in the layers they are of, and are shown there in front of what is in no group.
A group higher in the list covers the ones below it: Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ move it up or down, which is how two groups change places.
Double-click to go into it and edit what is in it; drag its bar to shift all of it in time, drag an end of the bar to trim or extend what is in it.
timeline.trimGroup.tip: What is in the group is trimmed or extended with it
timeline.trimGroup.gone: {0} object(s) lie outside altogether and are deleted when the mouse is let go
status.trimmedAway: {0} object(s) were left with nothing to show by the trim and have been deleted (undo brings them back)
group.enter.tip: Goes into the group like into a folder: the timeline lists what is in it. A double click on the group in the timeline or in the preview does the same
viewer.insideGroup: Editing the group "{0}"  (Esc goes back out)
props.selectedThings.note: They can be shifted in the timeline, copied and deleted together, or grouped once more. To edit the keyframes of one group, select it alone.
parse.groupPivot: The group's pivot or position is malformed
parse.groupCommandWithoutGroup: A group command comes before any group definition
parse.groupCommandKind: A group takes only M, MX, MY, S and R commands
parse.commandWithoutObject: A command comes before any Sprite or Animation declaration
parse.deepIndent: A command indented two levels has no L or T before it; it was read as a plain command
parse.legacyTerminalSprite: Ignored an invalid legacy sprite declaration at the end of the file
parse.paramLetter: The parameter of a P command must be H, V or A, not "{0}"
parse.tooFewValues: A {0} command needs at least {1} value(s); {2} found
parse.valueMultiple: A {0} command takes a multiple of {1} values; {2} found
parse.invalidValue: "{1}" is not a valid value for {0}
bake.loopTooLong: {0}: the loop unrolls into too many commands; the group's motion was not applied
bake.trigger: {0}: movement, scale and rotation inside a trigger do not inherit the object's group transforms
crash.recovered: The unsaved storyboard was autosaved. Reopen the project and use File > Restore autosave to get it back.
reference.note: Reads .osu files directly and refreshes changes, additions and deletions automatically. Without .osu files, only the shared storyboard is shown.
reference.missingText: The project's referenced beatmap directory cannot be found. Its path may have changed after sharing the project. Relink a directory on this computer, or unlink it to show only the shared storyboard.
reference.changing: Beatmap file is being saved; retry shortly: {0}
reference.unlinked: Beatmap reference unlinked; showing only the shared storyboard
reference.preserved: Beatmap refreshed; kept difficulty storyboards edited in the project: {0}
hitsound.laneVisibility.tip: Show or hide this lane's markers and enable or mute its sounds.
hitsound.brightnessFeedback.tip: Flash the corresponding hit-sound lane and marker during playback or click audition. Turn off to disable the visual feedback.
hitsound.recheck.tip: Show or hide the current difficulty's hit-object and hit-sound layers together. When enabled, hit sounds play even if osu! objects are hidden in the preview. Both layers are read-only and refresh automatically when the source .osu changes.
hitsound.readOnly: Read-only · Click a marker to preview its sound; also seeks while paused
hitsound.readOnlyFixed: Read-only · Click to preview the sound; use the wheel to seek. Clicks do not move the timeline
hitsound.legend:
Blue-grey: Normal / Amber: Soft / Coral: Drum
Marker: sample playback time; outline: explicit sample bank; red cross: missing file
hitsound.empty: No hit sounds in the current difficulty
hitsound.maniaUnsupported: Mania beatmaps are not supported yet
hitsound.explicit: Sample bank specified by the hit object
timeline.hitObject.selectionTip: Read-only · Click to select, drag to box-select. Ctrl-click to toggle or Ctrl-drag to add; Shift-click for a range, Ctrl+A to select all, Ctrl+C to copy an osu! timestamp. Double-click to locate in the osu! editor; Esc clears selection.
timeline.hitObject.openFailed: Could not open the osu! editor link: {0}
timeline.referenceTip: Read-only: click to seek; refreshes automatically when the source .osu changes
timeline.referenceFixedTip: Read-only: use the wheel to seek; clicks do not move the timeline. Refreshes automatically when the source .osu changes.
timeline.hitObjectEmpty: No hit objects in the current difficulty
timeline.osuIndicator.tip: Keep the playhead fixed left of centre while the timeline follows time. Click to select. With snap enabled, each wheel notch moves one snap tick; drag the scrollbar to seek as well.
simulation.title: Trigger simulation
simulation.offset.tip: When the event happens, in whole milliseconds.
assets.pathInside: Assets must be inside the assets folder of this project; parent-directory and external references are not allowed: {0}
timing.recheck.tip: Play one metronome click per beat using the project timing. Mutually exclusive with Hitsound Recheck. Click the selected option again to turn it off.
timing.brightnessFeedback.tip: Flash the beat and snap markers in the Timing track during playback or click audition.
timing.empty: No timing points. Add timing in project settings.
timing.readOnly: Read-only project beat grid. Click a marker to audition its metronome click.
timing.editBpm.tip: Double-click to edit BPM. Enter confirms; Escape cancels.
timing.editOffset.tip: Double-click to type the Offset in milliseconds. Enter confirms; Escape cancels.
timing.offsetNeighbours: Offset must stay between the neighbouring red lines: {0}.
timing.laneVisibility.tip: Show or mute the Timing lane and its clicks.
timing.deleteOffset: Delete the red line at the playhead
timing.invalidOffset: Offset must be an integer number of milliseconds (-2147483648 to 2147483647).
timing.invalidBpm: BPM must be greater than 0 and no more than 1000.
timing.invalidMeter: Beats per measure must be between 1 and 16.
timing.meter.tip: Beats per measure: the top number of an N/4 time signature (1–16). It sets where measures begin and which metronome beats are accented. For example, 3 means 3/4 and 4 means 4/4. Press Enter to apply.
timing.duplicateOffset: A red line already exists at this offset.
timing.bpmPrecision: BPM may have at most 3 decimal places.
timing.bpmPrecisionN: BPM may have at most {0} decimal places here; choose a higher BPM precision or round it.
timing.addOffset.bpmStep.tip: How exact the new red line's BPM may be: whole numbers (120), 1 decimal (120.5), 2 (120.25) or 3 (120.125). Choosing one rounds the BPM typed so far.
timeline.waveformStyle.tip: Waveform style. Changes appearance and remembers your selection.
timing.calculatorNote: Use the previous red line and current time as anchors. Beat count is estimated from the old BPM; adjust the subdivision count to match the music. Applying changes only the previous red line.
timing.calculatorBpm.tip: Type your own value to try it (more than 0, at most 1000, up to 3 decimals); the deviation below follows it. Suggested: {0:0.###}
timing.calculatorNoPrevious: No earlier red line. Choose a time after the first red line.
timing.calculatorInvalidSteps: Subdivision count must be a positive integer. At 1/4, 16 steps equal 4 beats.
timing.calculatorCannotAlign: Three-decimal BPM cannot align this target exactly. Adjust the step count or target time.
shortcut.timingList: Open Timing list (Timing check must be enabled)
shortcut.timingToggle: Add a red line at the playhead, or delete the one there (Timing check must be enabled)
shortcut.timingCalculator: Open the Timing calculator (Timing check must be enabled)
timing.copy.tip: Copy all red lines into the [TimingPoints] section of an .osu file. It can also be pasted straight into the osu! editor with Ctrl+V.
timing.list.currentNote: Highlighted: the red line in effect at the playhead
timing.deletePicked.tip: Removes the ticked red lines. Takes effect with OK, and can be undone.
timing.analysis.tip: Measure the average BPM and offset of the song, or of a part of it.
timing.analysis.title: Analyse BPM and offset
timing.analysis.note: Measures the average BPM and offset of the selected part of the main audio from its onsets. Drag on the waveform to choose the part, or type its start and end. It works best on a part with one steady BPM.
timing.analysis.integerHint: Close to a whole number: {0} BPM?
timing.analysis.notAi: This analysis is not AI timing: it uses signal-processing algorithms. See the references below.
timing.analysis.clearAdd.tip: Clear all timing of this project first, then add the result. Asks for confirmation first; can be undone.
timing.analysis.clearAdd.title: Clear and replace timing
timing.analysis.clearAdd.text:
This will clear all timing of the current project and replace it with the calculated result.
You can undo it. Continue?
timing.analysis.clearAdded: Cleared the old timing and added {0} red lines
timing.analysis.flagUnsteady: Parts marked ~ have scattered beats: drifting tempo or loose playing.
timing.analysis.flagLater: Parts marked > have beats slightly later than this timing.
timing.analysis.flagEarlier: Parts marked < have beats slightly earlier than this timing.
timing.analysis.flagNoBeat: Parts marked ? have few beats where this timing puts them: another timing section may start there.
timing.analysis.detail: Analysed {0} – {1} · {2}% of beats heard · spread {3} ms
timing.analysis.octave.tip: The beat may be counted at half or double this tempo; analyse again near that tempo.
timing.analysis.reference: The results are reference values only and must be checked by ear and eye before use.
timing.analysis.experimental: Experimental: for music played freely or speeding up and slowing down. Beats are followed one by one and miss more often; check every red line by ear after adding.
timing.analysis.tempoHint.tip: Leave empty to find it; with a BPM the beats are followed near that tempo (for example to avoid half or double tempo).
timing.analysis.tolerance.tip: A new red line starts when 8 beats in a row are off by more than this on average. Smaller values give more red lines.
timing.analysis.toleranceRange: The tolerance must be from {0} to {1} ms.
timing.analysis.minBeats.tip: The fewest beats one red line covers (1 allows a red line on every beat).
timing.analysis.align.tip: Every red line starts on a tick of this snap of the red line before it (the first on the red line before the range), so red lines always lie a whole number of snaps apart.
timing.analysis.bpmStep.tip: How exact each red line's BPM may be: whole numbers (120), 1 decimal (120.5), 2 (120.25) or 3 (120.125). Lower precision gives tidier BPMs but may need more red lines to follow the beats.
timing.analysis.meter.tip: Which beats are strong: 4/4 is strong, weak, medium, weak; 3/4 strong, weak, weak. Red lines go on the first beat of a bar and are set to this signature.
timing.analysis.calibration.tip: Added to the offsets the analysis finds, to correct its built-in calibration to your own preference: positive moves them later, negative earlier. Saved with your settings and used by both modes; changing it analyses again.
timing.analysis.calibrationRange: The calibration must be from {0} to {1} ms.
timing.analysis.kindCorrection.tip: Same BPM as the red line before, on the next downbeat: that red line had to start mid-bar, and a red line restarts the bar, so this one puts the bar lines back on the music's first beats.
timing.analysis.addAll.tip: Adds every red line above in the chosen time signature, corrections included, as one step that can be undone. Reference values: check each one afterwards.
timing.analysis.replace: Replace red lines in the range
timing.analysis.replace.tip: First removes the red lines already between start and end (in the same undo step).
timing.analysis.noAudio: The project has no main audio to analyse.
timing.analysis.overview.tip: Drag to choose the part to analyse; drag its edges to adjust.
timing.analysis.outOfSong: The time must be from 0 to {0} ms.
timing.analysis.order: The start must be before the end.
timing.analysis.tooShort: The part must be at least {0} ms long.
timing.analysis.knownBpm.tip: Leave empty to detect the BPM; with a BPM only the offset is measured.
timing.analysis.decodeFailed: The main audio could not be read.
timing.analysis.failed: The timing of this part could not be found: it may be too short, or have a drifting BPM or several timing sections.
timing.analysis.approximate: Only an approximate BPM could be found; take it as a guide.
timing.analysis.addLine.tip: Adds a red line with this BPM at this offset, on the first beat of a bar, in the chosen time signature (can be undone). It is a reference value: check it by ear afterwards.
timing.analysis.added: Added a {1} BPM red line at {0} ms.
timing.snapSound.tip: Only while checking Timing. Besides the beats, the metronome also clicks, more quietly, on every snap line of the current beat divisor.
timing.snapSound.hold: Hold Ctrl: while Timing check is on and this is unticked, sound on every snap for as long as Ctrl is held.
camera.title: Camera
camera.onlyRoot: Only the outermost group camera is used.
camera.disabledStatus: The camera of "{0}" is inactive: only the outermost group camera is used.
space.title: Space
space.owner: Space and camera come from the outermost group "{0}".
space.face.tip: Face the camera first, then apply the member’s own rotations.
space.z.tip: Depth: larger is farther away. Members are flat cards at different depths; pictures themselves are never drawn in perspective.
